test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 8 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A hallow spherical shell is made of a metal of density 6 g/cm³. Its internal and external radii are 8 cm and 9 cm, respectively. What is the weigh (in kg) of the shell (take π = (22)/(7))?
solution:
**Given:**

Density of the metal (ρ) = 6 g/cm³

Internal radius (r) = 8 cm

External radius (R) = 9 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a hollow sphere = (4)/(3)pi (R³ - r³)

Mass = Volume × Density

Weight (in kg) = Mass (in g) / 1000

**Calculation:**

Volume of the hollow spherical shell = (4)/(3) times (22)/(7) times (9³ - 8³)

⇒ Volume = (4)/(3) times (22)/(7) times (729 - 512)

⇒ Volume = (4)/(3) times (22)/(7) times 217

⇒ Volume = (4 times 22 times 217)/(3 times 7)

⇒ Volume = (88 times 217)/(21)

⇒ Volume = (19096)/(21) cm³

Mass of the shell = Volume × Density

⇒ Mass = (19096)/(21) × 6 g

⇒ Mass = (114576)/(21) g

Weight of the shell in kg = Mass in g / 1000

⇒ Weight = (114576)/(21 times 1000) kg

⇒ Weight = (114576)/(21000) kg

⇒ Weight = 5.456 kg

**∴ The weight of the shell is 5.456 kg.**
